title: Generalized People Diversity: Learning a Human Perception-Aligned Diversity Representation for People Images
measurement_description: The paper measures how well image ranking systems and vision-language representation spaces (specifically the proposed PATHS method) surface diverse representations of people. Regarding religion, it evaluates human perceptions of diversity when encountering markers of religious/cultural identity (like wearing a hijab) versus other traits (like skin tone) and tests whether the embedding models correctly align with these human preferences.
findings: The study found that human annotators heavily prioritize elements of cultural or religious attire, such as a hijab, over variations in skin tone when assessing the diversity of a group of images. The proposed perception-aligned PATHS model successfully captured this human preference by appropriately boosting images featuring religious attire (hijabs) during ranking, whereas baseline methods often failed to do so.
